title: Navratri. Dancing the garba.
lines: She lives in Antwerp, but her family comes from Gujarat, in India.
It's a big festival that lasts nine evenings.
They dance for Durga, the goddess who is very strong and brave.
She has lots of arms and she protects everyone from evil.
Mummy has bought a beautiful dress for Riya.
It's red and green and has little mirrors sewn onto it.
When Riya moves, the little mirrors sparkle like little stars.
The dress is called a chaniya choli.
Riya also gets bangles, lots of them, that jingle when she shakes her arm.
And a sparkly jewel for her forehead.
Daddy puts on a long, colourful kurta.
Her little brother Arjun has an orange kurta and a little turban.
Grandma puts on a beautiful sari.
They drive to a big hall.
There are lots of people from Gujarat there, from all over Belgium.
Everyone is wearing their most beautiful clothes.
In the middle of the hall there's a little altar with a statue of Durga.
Everyone sings, and the priest waves a little dish with a flame.
The people make big circles around the altar.
Grandma taught her in the living room.
Riya dances in the circle, with Grandma on one side and Mummy on the other.
Dum dum da-dum, dum dum da-dum!
Even Arjun dances along, a bit wobbly, with his little turban crooked.
After the garba comes the dandiya.
Pretty sticks, decorated with red and gold ribbons.
You tap your sticks together and against your partner's sticks.
Then she turns around and dances with the next person.
A boy in a green kurta.
An old man with a grey beard, who can dance really fast.
Riya laughs so hard that she almost drops her sticks.
Grandma, asks Riya, why do we dance?
Long ago there was an evil demon.
Then the goddess Durga came, on her lion.
She fought for nine days and nine nights.
And on the tenth day she defeated the demon.
That's why we dance for nine nights.
To celebrate that good wins over bad.
Dhokla, which is soft and yellow and a little bit sour.
It's late when they drive home.
Arjun is already asleep in his car seat.
Riya looks out of the window at the city lights.
